_comment: Curated alarm-name -> citation registry read by scripts/check_alarm_citations.py (#1959). Every CloudWatch alarm that has been in ALARM >72h must have an entry here (exact AlarmName key) naming the incident row or issue that explains it, or the /wrap gate flags it by name. Since #2912 the same holds for an alarm that FIRED AND CLEARED within the last 72h (episode start and end both in-window, read from describe-alarm-history) — a flap between wraps is invisible to current-state duration by construction, so it needs an entry or an explicit --decoded line just like a standing red. Add an entry the same session a new long-red alarm (or flap) is triaged; remove/replace one once the underlying issue closes AND the alarm has actually cleared live. Since #2996 a citation that names a `#N` must name an issue that is still OPEN: the gate reads `gh issue view` for every currently-lit alarm's citation and flags a dead reference, because a citation string is not an owner (measured 2026-08-22: 4 of 7 entries pointed at closed issues, 3 of them on lit alarms). A citation with NO `#N` is never flagged by that check — a dated, self-clearing state is honestly cited in prose — but the 14-day `issueless_ancient_reds` rule still forces a `#N` past that tenure. PRUNE an entry when its alarm recovers.

token-alarm-genesis-window-active.citation: dated self-clearing window, expires 2026-08-24 — no issue, by design
token-alarm-genesis-window-active.note: Re-pointed 2026-08-22 (#2996): the previous citation #2116 closed 2026-08-07 'partial'. This alarm is CORRECT and needs no owner: `lambdas/common/token_alarm_window.py` sets TOKEN_ALARM_GENESIS_WINDOW = ('2026-08-16', '2026-08-24'), a dated window around the cycle-14 genesis (2026-08-17), and the 1/0 gauge is 1 for its duration by construction. It SELF-CLEARS on 2026-08-24 with no deploy and no manual step; prune this entry then. Deliberately prose rather than a `#N` — filing an issue for a designed, dated state would be manufacturing an owner for something that is working. If it is still lit after 2026-08-24, that IS a defect and needs one.

cost-metric-drift-sustained.note: Expected RED from ~7 days after its first deploy: the alarm states a true, known condition. CostMetricDriftRatio has held ~1.37 since 2026-08-19 (measured live, #2883's 2026-08-20 comment) against the 1.15 acceptance bar — the residual self-report undercount (#2883 box 2: un-instrumented Bedrock callers outside Lambda, e.g. CI runners without AWS_LAMBDA_FUNCTION_NAME, plus partial cache-token capture) is still open. The alarm exists precisely so this residual cannot rot silently the way #357's regression did. Remove this entry when box 2 lands the ratio < 1.15 for a full week AND the alarm has actually cleared live.

budget-tier-sustained-7d.note: Re-pointed 2026-08-22 (#2996) from #2734, which closes: its projection half was resolved by measurement (mtd $124.80, projected $162.60 vs the $200 August ceiling = 81%; September at the measured $4.05/day projects $121.50 vs the permanent $150 base = 81% — neither month overruns, so the accept/cut/extend trilemma had no live premise). WHAT REMAINS IS THE ALARM'S CUT, and #2989 owns it: ADR-133 derived the $150 base from a measured steady state of $4.12/day = $123.60/mo = 82.4% of $150, which is INSIDE band 1 (73-87%). This alarm fires when the tier never returns to 0 across a week, so it alarms on the DESIGNED steady state. Band 0 would require daily spend <= $3.66.

qa-smoke-failures.note: Re-pointed 2026-08-22 (#2996): the previous citation #1921 closed 2026-08-01 and described the smoke oracle's deploy_health/content_truth partitioning, not this red. MEASURED live cause: the nightly FAIL line is `[content_truth] Semantic Recall / recall:corpus_freshness: 1 published installment(s) MISSING from the recall corpus: 2026-08-18` — which is exactly #2977, open. FailCount >= 1 on all 8 days measured (2026-08-14 through 08-21; daily max 1-3). Remove this entry when #2977 ships and FailCount reaches 0.

qa-smoke-warnings.note: Re-pointed 2026-08-22 (#2996): the previous citation #2912 closed 2026-08-22 and shipped the flap gate; it never explained this red. Lit since 2026-08-20 11:03 PT with WarnCount nonzero on 7 of 8 days. The open question #2997 owns: every `[QA] WARN` line logged in the last 28h is tagged `[chronic]` (which #1958 routes to the NON-alarmed ChronicWarnCount) and the one readable EMF summary line reports WarnCount 0 / ChronicWarnCount 7 — so the metric and the run's own log disagree, and the metric carries no dimensions to attribute a datapoint to a producer.

ingest-liveness-unhealthy.note: FLAP, not a standing red (#2912 detector caught it 2026-08-22). Fired and cleared inside one 72h window, so current-state duration is structurally blind to it. Investigated live this session: UnhealthySourceCount last landed a datapoint on 2026-08-20 while pipeline-health-check logged '16 pass, 0 fail' 2.2h before the wrap — the alarm was lit on a two-day-old datapoint describing a state the producer no longer reports. Root cause is the #2976 class: Period=86400 with the metric emitted only on the unhealthy path, so the alarm cannot fall as fast as the system recovers. Remove this entry when #2976 lands the healthy-path emission AND re-cuts the period; if it flaps again BEFORE that, the flap count is the signal — do not re-cite, add it to #2976 as evidence.

weekly-signal-delivery-heartbeat.citation: arming transition of the #2820 dead-man 2026-08-21 — not a delivery failure
weekly-signal-delivery-heartbeat.note: Kept 2026-08-22 (#2996). The alarm is OK, but #2912's flap check reads a 72h window and this alarm's only episode is inside it: describe-alarm-history shows INSUFFICIENT_DATA -> ALARM at 2026-08-21 20:44 PT and ALARM -> OK at 21:44 PT — one hour, immediately after #2820 deployed the WeeklySignalSent dead-man (treat_missing=BREACHING, so a freshly created alarm with no datapoints is ALARM by construction until the first one lands). No signal was missed. THE PRUNE RULE, corrected: remove a recovered alarm's entry once it has been OK for longer than the flap window (72h), not the moment it clears — pruning on recovery alone trades a stale entry for a flap-gate red, which is what happened while writing this. Prune after 2026-08-24 21:44 PT if still OK.
